text: CommonReel helps two to four adults choose a film for the same movie night. This is a constructed four-person group in the running application. Each person can optionally choose one to three films they explicitly like. Watching history only means watched. The catalog now contains two hundred and forty-seven verified Wikidata films.

title: No match. No silent relaxation.
note:
Limits stay hard
No horror. No musicals.
No automatic relaxation
text: Tonight, the room has eighty-one minutes, three US subscription services, and recorded vetoes for horror and musicals. Nothing qualifies. CommonReel keeps those boundaries. It does not silently relax a veto, assume an unknown title is unseen, or invent streaming access to force a recommendation.

title: What if we had 15 more minutes?
note:
0 to 19 eligible
15 extra minutes
Cache only. Room unchanged.
text: Instead, ask: what if we had fifteen more minutes? The free local Qwen model calls the real runtime preview tool through our MCP server. Go checks the complete catalog twice using current cached supply. In this recording, eighty-one to ninety-six minutes changes zero eligible films to nineteen. Only six new candidates are displayed; the count is calculated before truncation. The preview makes no supplier request and changes no room inputs.

title: Apply explicitly. Stay in sync.
text: Applying is a separate page action. Only this button changes the saved runtime. The other local-network client receives the new ninety-six-minute limit. Previous candidates and responses are cleared. A concurrent room edit, changed supply, or expired cache invalidates the preview rather than applying an outdated suggestion.

text: Now the shortlist includes Inside Out Two, listed on Disney Plus in the United States. The card shows its runtime, source check time, and partial preference evidence. Ranking still uses the original minimum-and-mean estimate. A streaming listing does not confirm anyone's account entitlement.

title: Record. Recheck. Save.
note:
4 / 4 recorded
Refresh supply, then commit
Group-recorded choice
text: Propose the film, then record a response for every member entry. Anyone holding the invitation may record for someone else, so this is a group-recorded choice. Saving is blocked until all four entries accept. The server refreshes the film's supply before committing, and preserves the choice after reload.
